s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive skin condition with itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Dome-shaped, red papules and nodules on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes in the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
key_facts: 12-year history of itchy eruptions over the whole body
Nodules appeared on the upper back 1 year previously and gradually increased in number and size
Patient denied a family history of inherited ichthyosis or atopy
Physical examination revealed extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Several 0.5- to 1-cm, dome-shaped, red papules and nodules were found on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes were observed on the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
Routine blood tests, biochemistry analyses, and peripheral blood flow cytometry tests were within normal limits
DNA analysis from paraffin sections showed clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor
Biopsy from back nodules showed atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis and extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive skin condition with itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy, consistent with clinical presentation and histopathology findings

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor and atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy, along with clonal T-cell population, makes this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Granulomatous slack skin disease
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology findings of atrophy of the epidermis and dense infiltrate of lymphocytes are consistent with this rare condition

shortlist.label: Pagetoid reticulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism and clonal T-cell population supports this diagnosis, although it is a rare condition

raw.rationale: The patient's 12-year history of itchy eruptions, presence of dome-shaped nodules on the upper back, and histopathology showing atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis and extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis are consistent with Mycosis fungoides. The clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor and immunohistochemical staining positive for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad, Mycosis fungoides is a specific type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and atypical cells in the peripheral blood, which is not the case here

rejected.label: Granulomatous slack skin disease
rejected.why: Characterized by granulomatous infiltrate and slack skin, which is not described in the patient's presentation

rejected.label: Pagetoid reticulosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with localized lesions and a distinct pagetoid appearance on histology, which is not consistent with the patient's widespread eruptions and histopathology
